subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may this migration delete them on the first write after upgrade?
rationale: Config backups are both recovery and sensitive-data artifacts, and the shipped numeric ring is documented and present in the latest release, so deleting those files is a product and upgrade-compatibility choice rather than an automation-only cleanup.

options.title: Require upgrade-safe migration
options.body: Keep the PR open but require preserving or converting `.bak.1` through `.bak.4` until bounded retention is safely replenished, plus proof for fresh and upgrade paths.

options.title: Accept first-write pruning
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept deleting legacy numeric backups, but the PR should document that upgrade behavior and prove the remaining recovery path is acceptable.

options.title: Pause for broader backup layout
options.body: Pause this naming-only PR if the dedicated backup-directory design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20460 should own the naming and migration policy together.

recommendation.title: Require upgrade-safe migration
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open but require preserving or converting `.bak.1` through `.bak.4` until bounded retention is safely replenished, plus proof for fresh and upgrade paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent config backup/recovery history and prior review context make this the best available owner for the upgrade-behavior decision.
